program_name: Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics (commonly abbreviated 'EPE' in unibz course codes and OFA rules). Official Italian name: 'Corso di laurea in Economia, Politica ed Etica'; official German name: 'Bachelor in Ökonomie, Politik und Ethik' — both used in the signed ranking-list documents. Faculty of Economics and Management. Degree course director: Prof. Ivo De Gennaro.
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English), and unlike a nominally trilingual programme the three languages are genuinely and unavoidably interleaved across compulsory courses. unibz publishes no official percentage split, but the 2026/27 course-offering page states the language of instruction for every single course, which allows an exact count. Of the 17 subject courses published for 2026/27 (excluding the six 'as a Foreign Language' courses and the 0 CP preparatory/OFA modules): ENGLISH — Macroeconomics (8), History of Economic Thought (6), Comparative Politics (8), Public Economics (7), Introduction to Academic Writing (3), Microeconomics (8), Information Systems and Data Management (2), Principles of Philosophy 1 (8), Mathematics for EPE (12, both modules) = 62 CP; ITALIAN — Statistics for EPE (8), Growth and Development Economics (7), Data Science for Social Sciences (8), Econometrics (7), Public Law and Fundamental Rights module (6) = 36 CP; GERMAN — Principles of Philosophy 2 (8), Applied Econometrics (7), Business Administration (8), European Law module (6) = 29 CP. That is roughly 49% English, 28% Italian, 23% German by credit. The 12 CP 'European and Public Law' course is itself split IT + DE. Free-choice electives for 2026/27 follow the same pattern (English: Introduction to Public Policy, Wine Economics, Theory of International Relations, The Economics of Climate Change; German: Philosophy of Economics, Industrial Economics; Italian: Labour Law, Ethics Science Art, Contract Law). Compulsory language courses: two 'Foreign Language 1 / 2 — Specialized Language Course' slots (3+3 CP, year 1) and two 'Advanced Specialized Language course' slots (3+3 CP, year 2); exams must be taken in 2 of the 3 languages and the main language of instruction of your own secondary school may NOT be chosen. Students who graduated in a language other than the three unibz teaching languages must nominate the two languages in which they will sit these exams. [uncertain — the credit percentages are computed from the 2026/27 course-offering listing, which shows only the lectures currently offered and does not include third-year courses; unibz itself publishes no language weighting]
campus: Bozen-Bolzano (main campus, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano), Faculty of Economics and Management. Single campus — no NOI Techpark, Brixen-Bressanone, Bruneck-Brunico, Trento or Innsbruck component. A study period abroad at a partner university (min. 20 – max. 80 credit points) via Erasmus+/bilateral agreements/free mover is compulsory, as is an internship (4 CP in year 3).
degree_class: L-33 (Scienze economiche / Economics). Confirmed verbatim on the 2026/27 brochure 'At a glance': 'Bachelor class: L-33'. Note that the double-enrolment rule quoted in the admission PDF uses L-18 only as a generic example; this programme is L-33, which means it can legally be combined with an L-18 programme under the two-programme rule.
offered_in_2026_27: YES — fully offered, and it is one of the few Faculty of Economics and Management programmes still ACCEPTING APPLICATIONS at the verification date. All three intake windows ran: Early Bird and Late Application both completed with signed ranking lists published (70 EU + 1 non-EU admitted in Early Bird; 33 EU admitted in Late), and the Additional Application Session (18/08 – 04/09/2026, EU citizens only) is explicitly listed as 'Application possible' for this programme. This is a direct contrast with the sister programme Bachelor in Economics and Management, which is listed as 'Application NOT offered' for the additional session. As of 2026-08-29 the additional-session window is still OPEN (closes 04/09/2026 at noon local time).
is_new_programme: No — an established programme, not a new 2026 launch. Supporting evidence: a published grade-statistics page exists for the L-33 degree (https://www.unibz.it/en/faculties/economics-management/bachelor-economics-politics-ethics/grade-statistics-l-33), which requires multiple graduated cohorts; the brochure points prospective students to AlmaLaurea statistics on 'graduates' satisfaction and their employability'; the faculty maintains separate 'Course Offering – enrolled from 2025' and 'enrolled before 2025' curricula; and course pages exist under both /2025/ and /2026/ paths. The 2026/27 selection criteria were approved by routine annual Faculty Council resolution (no. 142 of 15.09.2025), not by a new-programme establishment act. [uncertain — unibz does not publish the first intake year anywhere, and the ranking-list index retains only the current year's documents, so the exact founding year could not be established]
majors_tracks_study_plans: Two majors (curricula), both leading to the same L-33 degree in economics: (1) POLITICS AND ETHICS MAJOR and (2) ECONOMICS MAJOR. The choice is made at the END OF THE SECOND YEAR, not at application — years 1 and 2 are identical for both majors, so applicants do not select a track when applying. The Politics and Ethics curriculum 'maintains the integrative perspectives of political science and philosophical and ethical analysis', while the Economics curriculum 'is mainly focused on the perspective and methods of economic science'. Shared years 1–2 (180 ECTS total over 3 years): year 1 — Microeconomics 8, Macroeconomics 8, Mathematics for EPE 12 (modules A+B, 6+6), Comparative Politics 8, Principles of Philosophy 1 8, Business Administration 8, History of Economic Thought 6, Foreign Language 1 and 2 (3+3), Information Systems and Data Management 2; year 2 — Statistics for EPE 8, European and Public Law 12 (Public Law and Fundamental Rights 6 + European Law 6), one complementary subject from {Principles of Philosophy 2, Data Science for Social Sciences} 8, typical subject 1 from {Growth and Development Economics, Public Economics} 7, typical subject 2 from {Applied Econometrics, Econometrics} 7, Introduction to Academic Writing 3, two Advanced Specialized Language courses (3+3), Free Choice 6. Year 3 POLITICS AND ETHICS — Nature and Society 7, Economic Policy and Institutions 7, Environmental and Resource Economics 7, Responsible and Transformative Decision Making 7, Political Theory 8, Italian and European Economic Law 6, Internship 4, Free Choice 6, Bachelor Thesis 5. Year 3 ECONOMICS — Political Economics 7, Economic Policy: Theory and Practice 8, International Economics 7, Labor Economics 7, Financial Markets and Institutions for EPE 7, Italian and European Banking and Financial Law 6, Internship 4, Student's choice subjects 6, Bachelor Thesis 5. Part-time enrolment is available as an administrative variant with a reduced annual course load and full access to services; it is chosen after enrolment (in October), not during the application. No dual-study or 4-year variant.
english_only_accessibility: EFFECTIVELY CLOSED for a candidate who can only certify English — and for this programme the barrier is stronger than the admission rule alone, because it is also curricular. (1) ADMISSION GATE: B2 is required in the FIRST language and B2 in the SECOND language, chosen from German, Italian and English. Someone with only English fills at most one of the two positions and is excluded from the procedure before ranking. This is not theoretical — the 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list excludes 13 EU/equivalent applicants and 1 non-EU applicant by name-ID 'for not meeting the language requirements for admission', and the Late list excludes 7 more on the same ground. Notably, 13 language-excluded EU applicants is larger than the entire gap between the 70 admitted and the single waiting-list candidate: language, not grades, is what filtered this cohort. (2) CURRICULAR GATE, specific to EPE and decisive: several COMPULSORY courses are taught only in Italian or only in German and have no English section — Statistics for EPE (8 CP, Italian), Business Administration (8 CP, German), and European and Public Law (12 CP, split Italian + German). Worse, two of the year-2 choice pairs offer no English option at all: the complementary subject is either Principles of Philosophy 2 (German) or Data Science for Social Sciences (Italian), and typical subject 2 is either Applied Econometrics (German) or Econometrics (Italian). An English-only student therefore could not assemble a valid year-2 study plan even if admitted. (3) Add the compulsory 'Foreign Language' course slots, which must be taken in 2 of the 3 languages and cannot include the applicant's own school language. A Turkish or other international applicant needs a certified B2 in German OR Italian in addition to English, and realistically needs to build toward working proficiency in both. Classification: effectively-closed.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with competitive ranking. No entrance examination, no TOLC, no TOLC-E, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT/GRE, no interview and no portfolio. Selection is a document- and grade-based dossier evaluation carried out by the Admission Committee on the basis of self-declared secondary-school grades plus language-certificate bonus points. Applications are submitted online through the unibz Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup/). Separate quotas and procedures apply to (1) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (2) non-EU citizens living abroad. Legal basis: selection criteria approved by Faculty of Economics Faculty Council Resolution no. 142 of 15.09.2025. Admission Committee for 2026/27: Prof. Ivo De Gennaro (President), Prof. Roberto Farneti and Prof. Paolo Roberti (members). Administrative appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Administrative Court of Bolzano within 60 days of notification or publication.
academic_requirements: A secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system, OR an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if it was obtained after 12 YEARS of education AND at least the LAST TWO YEARS were attended within that foreign school system — unibz gives the Irish Leaving Certificate as the counter-example ('it is not enough to attend one year and obtain the foreign certificate'). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes additional specific requirements on holders of certain qualifications, with American high school diplomas and British and Greek certificates named explicitly; applicants in those categories are told to contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service) before applying. There are NO subject prerequisites, no minimum GPA gate other than the 21/33 ranking threshold, and no prior ECTS/SSD credit requirement — the SSD-credit logic (INFO-01/A etc.) applies to unibz master admissions, not to this bachelor. Meeting the language requirements is itself a hard entry requirement: 'To be admitted, you must fulfil the language requirements indicated in the section Language requirements.' Under national rules, simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is allowed provided the two are not in the same degree class and differ in at least 2/3 of course content — since this programme is L-33, it may be paired with an L-18 programme. Candidates who have not yet graduated may apply and upload the diploma at enrolment. Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment, and only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.
entry_exam_or_test: NO admission entrance exam of any kind. unibz does not use its own subject test, TOLC-I, TOLC-E, CENT-S, SAT or GMAT/GRE for this programme; admission is purely dossier- and ranking-based on high-school grades plus language bonus points.

Language proficiency exams (OPTIONAL route, used only if you cannot prove your levels via diploma or a recognised certificate): organised online by the unibz Language Centre. 2026/27 Early Bird sittings 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 plus 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); Late Application sittings 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). Registration is done inside the application portal under 'enrol for language exams', which only becomes available after creating an application. IMPORTANT: only B2-level exams can be booked, so C1 (needed for bonus points) requires an external certificate. CRITICAL FOR THE ADDITIONAL SESSION: the Language Centre offers NO language exams for the additional application session — unibz instead recommends LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS 'as the results of these exams are generally available within a short period of time'.

Compulsory mathematics test — AFTER admission, not for admission. The faculty runs a preparatory course in mathematics in English before the first semester (2026/27: 21–25/09/2026) and every new student must sit a compulsory test at the end of it. A negative result or non-participation triggers OFA. Test topics: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Faculty-Economics/OFA-Topics26.pdf (published in English only). A 0 CP 'OFA-Mathematics' remedial module (course code 27361, taught in English) is listed in the semester 1 offering.

Third-language placement test — after admission, for students who cannot certify their third language. The result assigns the student to a language learning path aimed at reaching B2 as quickly as possible.
selection_scoring: Maximum 33 points; minimum 21/33 required for admission; the final score is rounded up or down. Component (a), max 30 points: the grade average of the last two AVAILABLE high-school years (the last two if the final year is already available, otherwise the two years preceding the final year), expressed in thirtieths. For each of those years the candidate supplies one mark for each of four subject areas — 1) Language (any, including modern and ancient), 2) Mathematics, 3) Humanities and Social Sciences (history, philosophy, politics, sociology, economics, law), 4) Natural and Technical Sciences (physics, chemistry, biology, geography, environmental studies, informatics) — plus 2 further marks from areas 1, 3 or 4. If no subject can be assigned to one of areas 1–4, a grade from another area may be substituted. EXCLUDED from the calculation: conduct (condotta/Betragen), religion, physical education, performing-arts subjects (instrumental music, singing, drama/theatre) and hospitality-sector subjects (cuisine, restaurant and bar service, oenology). Component (b), max 3 points: language bonus (see bonus_points). Tie-breakers: higher grade average first, then the younger applicant. Fallbacks: if grades for a year are not supplied the Committee assigns a score corresponding to 'sufficient merit' for that year; for school systems substantially different from the Italian one the Committee may evaluate final reports from years other than the last two; if the candidate already holds a university degree the Committee uses the university exam average. ACTUAL 2026/27 CUT-OFFS (competition signal — this programme is markedly less competitive than the sister Economics and Management degree): EARLY BIRD, EU/equivalent — 70 admitted, rank 1 score 33.00 (a perfect score), rank 70 and last admitted 21.27; the waiting list contained just ONE person (rank 71, 21.20); only 2 applicants were excluded for falling below the minimum (20.49 and 19.74); 13 further applicants were excluded for not meeting the language requirements. EARLY BIRD, non-EU living abroad — only 1 of the 4 available places was filled, at score 22.73, with 1 applicant excluded on language grounds. LATE APPLICATION, EU/equivalent — 33 admitted, rank 1 score 30.99, rank 33 and last admitted 21.24, NO waiting list at all and NO exclusions for insufficient score, meaning every language-eligible applicant who cleared 21/33 was admitted; 7 applicants were excluded on language grounds. Practical reading: the binding constraint for this programme is the language requirement, not the score — the effective cut-off sat essentially at the 21/33 floor in both sessions.
bonus_points: Maximum 3 bonus points, awarded solely for language proficiency ABOVE the level required for admission, on this scale: C1 + C1 + at least B2 = 3 points; C1 + C1 + B1 = 2.5 points; C1 + C1 = 2 points; at least B2 + B2 + B2 = 1 point; at least B2 + B2 + B1 = 0.5 points. Only language certificates recognised by the unibz Language Centre count, as do exams taken at the Language Centre provided a course for the requested level is offered — and since the Language Centre only examines at B2, the C1 tiers require an external recognised certificate. NO other bonus schemes exist for this programme: there is no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that is a Master in Software Engineering / Computing for Data Science mechanism), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance), and no startup-project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation). Given that the effective cut-off sat at roughly 21.2–21.3 in both 2026/27 sessions, the 3-point language bonus is proportionally large and can by itself decide admission.
portfolio_and_materials: None required. No portfolio, no video, no project proposal, no motivation letter, no CV and no reference letters form part of this admission procedure, and therefore no format or size limits (the 20 MB PDF portfolio, 2-page project proposal, 6,000-character motivation letter and 2-minute video limits used elsewhere at unibz do not apply here). The only uploads are: a valid ID card or passport (front and back), the online application form with self-declared grades, copies of the school report cards for any self-declared year completed abroad, official translations of those report cards into Italian, German or English where needed, optional language certificates, and the diploma (at application if already held, otherwise at enrolment).
interview: No interview. The admission procedure contains no oral or online interview stage at any point, for either EU or non-EU applicants, and no interview dates are published for this programme in any of the three 2026/27 sessions.
conditional_admission: Yes, in the bachelor sense: applicants who have not yet completed secondary school may apply and are ranked on the grades of the two years preceding the final year, uploading the diploma at enrolment rather than at application. The ECTS-threshold form of conditional admission (>=120 ECTS, or 140 for Data Analytics) does NOT apply here — that is a unibz master's mechanism. Financial protection: if you pay the first instalment to secure your place but then fail your secondary-school final exam, you ARE entitled to a refund; this is one of only two refund exceptions, the other being non-EU applicants abroad who cannot obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities in their country. Non-EU citizens living abroad are additionally admitted 'with reservation' (con riserva / mit Vorbehalt) on the ranking list, and the reservation is lifted only once the Italian consulate abroad sends official confirmation directly to unibz. A separate reservation applies to any applicant with a foreign qualification who has not yet uploaded the ARDI/CIMEA documentation: 'until you have uploaded the above documentation, you can only be admitted with reservation', and if the qualification is ultimately judged inadequate the applicant is excluded. Missing the fee-payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the next person on the ranking list is admitted.
ofa_rules: Yes — OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional study achievements) applies. OFA is assigned to any student who fails, or does not attend, the compulsory mathematics test held at the end of the September mathematics preparatory course. Three alternative ways to clear it: (1) pass the test offered at the end of the OFA exercise sessions, (2) pass the exam at the end of teaching module 1 of the 'Mathematics' course, or (3) pass the full mathematics exam (teaching module 1 + teaching module 2) within the first academic year. Consequence of not clearing OFA: the student is blocked from sitting the quantitative examinations of years 2 and 3 — for this programme specifically 'Statistics for EPE', 'Econometrics' and 'Data Science for Social Sciences' (note these differ from the Economics and Management list, which names Statistics, Financial Mathematics and the two Econometrics courses). A dedicated 0 CP 'OFA-Mathematics' module (code 27361, English) is offered in semester 1. Test topics: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Faculty-Economics/OFA-Topics26.pdf
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the language requirement is a HARD EXCLUSION GATE, not a scoring factor: 'the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. Requirements are defined by POSITION (1st/2nd/3rd language), not by which specific language: your first language is the one in which you have the highest proficiency, your third is the one in which you are weaker or an absolute beginner. Entry: B2 in the 1st language, B2 in the 2nd language, no level required in the 3rd. Exit (to graduate): C1 / C1 / B2, CEFR. Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and only RECOMMENDED (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. B1 in the third language is the minimum for sitting curricular exams in that language, and if the first semester is taught only in English while English is your third language, you must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January to sit all first-semester exams. Formalities: a certificate awarded by an Italian public institution is submitted as a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original. Free Language Centre courses target B1 in the third language by end of year 1 and B2 by end of year 2; extensive courses run 4 h/week during semesters and intensive courses 6 h/day between semesters, with a three-week September intensive block (2026/27: 01–18/09/2026, Mon–Fri, 6 h/day). A1 beginner courses are offered ONLY in that September window during the normal cycle, so absolute beginners must start there. ADDITIONAL-SESSION CAVEAT (relevant right now): applicants admitted through the additional session cannot attend the September intensive courses, the Language Centre runs no exams for that session, and A1 courses for them start only in mid-October 2026 with the standard path to B1 running October 2026 – September 2027; unibz 'strongly advises' additional-session beginners to acquire A1 in their third language before studies start. Higher-than-required levels earn up to 3 ranking bonus points.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 — 2nd language: B2 — 3rd language: no level required at entry. (Pattern B2/B2/none, the same as Economics and Management, and one step below the C1/B2 pattern used by Public Policy and Accounting and Finance.) Positions are self-assigned by proficiency across German, Italian and English, so any two of the three may occupy positions 1 and 2 — but note the curricular reality for this programme: compulsory courses exist in all three languages, so the 'third language' cannot in practice be neglected. Conditional follow-on requirements: B1 in the 3rd language to sit curricular examinations in that language, and B1 in English by mid-January if English is your 3rd language and your first semester is English-only. Because the unibz Language Centre only examines at B2 level, an applicant needing C1 for bonus points must present an external recognised certificate.
exit_levels: 1st language: C1 — 2nd language: C1 — 3rd language: B2 (CEFR). This is a graduation condition, so a student admitted at the minimum B2/B2/none must raise two languages to C1 and reach B2 in the third before graduating. The Language Centre's free course path is calibrated to it (B1 in the third language by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2). The curriculum reinforces this independently: two 'Foreign Language – Specialized Language Course' slots (3+3 CP, year 1) and two 'Advanced Specialized Language course' slots (3+3 CP, year 2) must be sat in 2 of the 3 offered languages, excluding the main language of instruction of the student's own secondary school. If the student already holds the required proficiency levels under the University Council's 'Guidelines on Multilingualism and Language Certificates' at the start of the programme, these language courses may be replaced by optional subjects up to a maximum of 6 CP — but the intention to do so must be declared at the start of the degree programme. Students from a Ladin school in South Tyrol must sit the English exams and choose between German and Italian for the others; students who graduated in a language other than the three unibz languages must nominate their two exam languages to the Faculty Secretariat.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. Special case flagged by unibz: if the first semester of the programme is taught only in English and English is your third language, you must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January in order to sit all curricular exams scheduled for the first semester. Students who cannot certify the third language on admission take a placement test after admission and are assigned a learning path aimed at reaching B2 as quickly as possible. For this programme the threshold has unusual practical bite, because compulsory first- and second-year courses are taught in Italian (Statistics for EPE, Public Law and Fundamental Rights) and in German (Business Administration, European Law): whichever of the three is a student's third language, they will meet compulsory coursework in it early.
proof_pathways: Four accepted routes, all handled inside the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams' (both available only after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'): (1) The main teaching language of your FINAL high-school year, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1. Ladin upper-secondary schools are recognised as B2 in German and Italian. For foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma you must also upload a letter or document from the school stating it. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; the same medium-of-instruction letter rule applies to foreign degrees; unibz graduates upload the Language Centre certificates obtained and/or declare the B2, B2+ or C1 exams they passed. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list (https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf); if it cannot be uploaded it may be sent by e-mail as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) A language exam organised by the unibz Language Centre — 2026/27 online sittings 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 plus 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026) for Early Bird, and 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026) for Late Application; only B2-level exams can be booked, and if you start your application outside a registration period you must return to the portal during one of the listed periods to register. NO Language Centre exams are held for the Additional Application Session — for that session unibz recommends LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS because results arrive quickly, and directs applicants to the recognised-certificates list to check which exams are also accepted in the online 'Home Edition' format. FIFTH PARTIAL ROUTE for foreign, bilingual and multilingual schools: if CEFR levels (B1/B2/C1) for German, Italian or English are explicitly stated on the graduation diploma AND all four skills were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the 2nd and/or 3rd language — upload the school leaving certificate under the respective language and the Language Centre decides on recognition.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 (Beschluss des Universitätsrates / Delibera del Consiglio dell'Università n. 16/2026), which is the header of the official recognised-certificates list. Core rules: (1) the certificate must assess ALL FOUR skills (reading, listening, speaking, writing) and be issued by the certification provider itself; (2) it must show a sufficient result in every skill as an overall grade, or the detailed per-skill assessment must appear on the certificate itself or in appropriate documentation from the issuer; (3) if no overall result or level is stated, the LOWEST level reached in any sub-skill determines the recognised level, provided that part was passed; (4) there is NO compensation for failed parts and no averaging unless the issuer itself provides for it; (5) certificates obtained as remote 'home edition' exams are NOT recognised except for those explicitly flagged in the list — a point that matters unusually much for the currently open additional session, where unibz simultaneously recommends fast-turnaround exams and tells applicants to check which ones are accepted in Home Edition format; (6) single-skill certificates combined from different organisations are not accepted; (7) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and exams from private educational providers, and placement-test results are not recognised; (8) certificates issued by individual lecturers, readers or teachers are not recognised; (9) DAAD certificates are explicitly NOT recognised. Validity: an international certificate must have been obtained within the last five years before submission, counted as the whole calendar year from 1 January. Items listed in the 'Further proofs / Ulteriori attestati / Weitere Nachweise' section have unlimited validity.
application_deadline_eu: THREE sessions were open for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment in 2026/27 — and unlike the sister Bachelor in Economics and Management, this programme DID take part in the third one. (1) EARLY BIRD — application 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). (2) LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only) — application 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08, by noon local time (28/05 - 08/07/2026). (3) ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU citizens only) — application 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04, by noon local time (18/08 - 04/09/2026), confirmed as 'Application possible' for this programme on the official additional-session page. AS OF THE VERIFICATION DATE 2026-08-29 THIS THIRD WINDOW IS STILL OPEN, closing in a few days on 2026-09-04 at noon; studies start in October 2026. Applicants excluded in one session may re-apply in the next (the ranking lists show this happening: several applicant IDs excluded on language grounds in Early Bird reappear as admitted in the Late list, e.g. IDs 152358, 151133, 156024, 152911, 152193 and 153183). EU applicants may also apply to more than one study programme. Note that 2027/28 dates are not yet published.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (Early Bird; unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). Non-EU citizens living outside Italy have NO Late Application and NO Additional Session — 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' A non-refundable EUR 50 application fee applies. Downstream 2026/27 dates matched the Early Bird calendar: ranking list published by 2026-05-27, first instalment by 2026-06-05 (noon), enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 (noon). Universitaly pre-enrolment is mandatory after paying the first instalment, and admission on the ranking list is granted 'with reservation' until the Italian consulate confirms directly to unibz. For the 2026/27 cycle this window has closed; a non-EU applicant living abroad who discovers the programme now cannot use the open additional session, which is restricted to EU citizens and those given parity of treatment.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU-equivalent and therefore gain access to the Late Application and Additional sessions and the much larger EU quota. (1) Citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State. (2) Non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay (permesso di soggiorno) under article 39 paragraph 5 of Decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998 — issued for WORK, FAMILY reasons, political or humanitarian ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. They apply directly to the University and must submit a copy of the valid permit; if it has expired, a renewal request must be attached. CRITICAL FOR TURKISH AND OTHER NON-EU APPLICANTS: 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not sufficient.' If the permit is not uploaded in the application portal the applicant is automatically reclassified as a non-EU citizen living abroad and pushed into the Italian-consulate procedure with the much smaller quota — 4 places instead of 80, and a single application window that has already closed for 2026/27.
places_quotas: Three separate published numbers for 2026/27, 84 in total. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: 70 in Early Bird + 10 in Late Application = 80. Non-EU citizens living abroad: 4, Early Bird only. The brochure's 'At a glance' box states the same total as 'Places available: 80 EU + 4 non-EU'. Any Early Bird places left unfilled by EU/equivalent candidates roll over into the Late Application round for EU/equivalent candidates. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN 2026/27: Early Bird admitted exactly 70 EU/equivalent candidates with a waiting list of just ONE person, and filled only 1 of the 4 non-EU places (score 22.73), with 1 further non-EU applicant excluded on language grounds; the Late session then admitted 33 EU candidates — far above its nominal quota of 10, because unclaimed Early Bird places rolled over — with no waiting list and no score-based exclusions at all. Places clearly remained after that, which is why the Additional Application Session was opened for this programme. NO QUOTA IS PUBLISHED FOR THE ADDITIONAL SESSION: the official page lists only 'Application possible' and states no number of available places. General rules: missing the payment deadline means automatic exclusion and the next candidate on the list is admitted; missing the enrolment deadline has the same effect. A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure a maximum of two places by paying the designated rate twice. Paying does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol, except if you fail your secondary-school final exam or, as a non-EU applicant abroad, cannot obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities. Enrolling early is recommended so that incomplete documents can still be corrected before the deadline. Ranking lists are valid for the respective academic year only. Once enrolled, the faculty fee calendar differs from the admission calendar: first instalment due 13/10/2026 and second by 31/03/2027.

required_documents: AT APPLICATION, uploaded in the unibz Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): (1) a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (2) the completed online application form including self-declaration of the grades for the four subject areas plus two extra subjects for each of the two relevant high-school years (for German secondary schools, the 'Jahreszeugnis' grades, or if unavailable the average of the two 'Halbjahreszeugnisse' with decimal place); (3) a copy of the relevant school report cards for any self-declared year completed abroad; (4) the official translation of the school report cards into Italian, German or English where needed; (5) optionally, language certificates, both to prove the entry levels and to earn bonus points; (6) the diploma of the qualification if already obtained (otherwise at enrolment); (7) for parity-of-treatment applicants, a copy of the valid Italian permit to stay (plus a renewal request if expired). Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Once sent, the application cannot be modified, and forms that are filled in but not correctly submitted are disregarded. AT ENROLMENT, for a foreign secondary-school qualification: the secondary school diploma; an official translation of the diploma into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English); plus the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. NOTE: the structured 'study career' Excel template that unibz requires for master's applications is NOT part of this bachelor procedure. Students transferring from another Italian university must additionally submit a copy of the transfer application filed at their previous university to the Student Office at the start of the academic year. unibz performs its own checks on foreign qualifications and reserves the right to request additional documents in case of doubt; a student without a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment.
application_fee: EUR 50, payable ONLY by non-EU citizens living abroad. It is an administration fee and is expressly non-refundable. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment pay no application fee, including in the currently open additional session.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/economics-management/fees — EUR 1,200 per year for students within the normal programme length, split into two instalments of EUR 600. The 1st instalment includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) and, during the admission procedure, is the payment that secures the admitted place (2026/27 admission deadlines: 05/06/2026 Early Bird, 06/08/2026 Late, 25/09/2026 Additional). Once enrolled, the Faculty of Economics and Management fee calendar is 1st instalment by 13/10/2026 and 2nd instalment by 31/03/2027 — the admission PDF states this more loosely as 'by March of the following year'. Students two or more years beyond the normal programme length (fuori corso) pay EUR 1,500 (EUR 900 + EUR 600); students up to one year beyond still pay the standard EUR 600 + EUR 600. Late payment of the second instalment incurs a EUR 30 fine and blocks the online account, exam registration and transfers; unpaid fees also block transfer to other universities or programmes. Interruption years are excluded from the fuori corso calculation but repeated years count towards the higher tier. No refund on drop-out, interruption or exclusion. Full exemption (paying only the EUR 16 stamp) applies to students with a disability recognised under art. 3 para. 1 of Law 104/1992 or a disability of 66% or more — the health-authority certificate must be handed in at the start of the academic year — and to foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Holders of a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano receive a refund of the tuition fees, usually in March–April, though late-payment fines are not refunded.
scholarships_grants: (1) Provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano/South Tyrol, applied for through the provincial Office for Higher Education Support (Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario), in three categories: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships and postgraduate study grants. Holders also receive a refund of their unibz tuition fees. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS, quoted from the unibz Study Guide: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — so a first-year non-EU student arriving on a study visa is effectively excluded from it in year 1. (2) Merit-based scholarships from the second year onwards. (3) Tuition-fee exemption for Italian-government scholarship holders and for students with a recognised disability (see tuition_or_fees_link). (4) The student associations sh.asus and the South Tyrolean Students Association assist with the application forms. No programme-specific scholarship is advertised for the Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics on its own page. Source: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants [uncertain — the unibz study-grants page states no euro amounts at all and refers applicants to the provincial website; the frequently cited range of roughly EUR 1,680–6,960 per year comes from other unibz material and could not be confirmed against the current 2026/27 provincial call]
credential_recognition: Required at ENROLMENT for holders of a foreign secondary-school qualification, in three tiers. (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate: Statement of Correspondence of the secondary-school diploma, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database – Italy). (b) Non-EU countries that ARE signatories of the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Correspondence from ARDI PLUS Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA (Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence). (c) Non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA PLUS Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. In all cases the diploma itself and an official Italian translation must be uploaded, the translation not being needed for diplomas issued in German or English. Until this documentation is uploaded the applicant can only be admitted with reservation; if the qualification is judged inadequate for enrolment the applicant is excluded. The 12-years-of-education rule and the last-two-years-in-that-school-system rule also apply. unibz performs its own checks and may request additional documents, and an invalid admission qualification can lead to exclusion by Rector's decree even after enrolment. The 180-ECTS Diploma Supplement evidence mentioned in the field definition applies to master's admissions, not to this bachelor. Turkey is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so Turkish applicants fall under tier (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. [uncertain — the tier assignment for Turkey is inferred from Turkey's Lisbon Convention membership; unibz publishes the rule by tier and not as a country-by-country table, so Turkish applicants should confirm with apply@unibz.it]
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply in the single Early Bird window with the EUR 50 fee -> ranking list published, with admission granted 'with reservation' (con riserva / mit Vorbehalt) -> pay the 1st instalment to secure the place -> start the visa application on the Universitaly portal, which is MANDATORY ('otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol') and on which only ONE study programme may be selected -> the Italian diplomatic/consular authorities in your country issue the study/university entry visa and send official confirmation directly to unibz, which lifts the reservation -> enrol at unibz. After arrival: under Italian law the residence permit (permesso di soggiorno) must be applied for within 8 WORKING DAYS of arrival — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival — and once obtained the permit must be handed in at the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay but cannot obtain the necessary enrolment documents from the Italian authorities in their country are entitled to a refund. Proof of means of subsistence for the visa (general unibz guidance, not restated in this programme's PDF): roughly EUR 800 per month of living costs in Bozen-Bolzano excluding tuition, with a total of at least EUR 36,000 to be demonstrated for a bachelor programme, and the budget should also cover health insurance and visa costs; student work is capped at 20 hours per week / 1,040 hours per year. Practical note for this programme: the non-EU route is quantitatively marginal here — 4 places offered, 1 filled in 2026/27, and 1 of the 2 non-EU applicants who reached the ranking stage was excluded for not meeting the language requirements.
official_call_url: No separate call, manifesto or bando document is published in English for this programme — the admission-information PDF functions as the official call. source_quotes: Places (admission-information PDF, 'Available places'): 'EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — Early Bird Application: 70; Late Application: 10. Non-EU citizens (living abroad) — Early Bird Application: 4.'

Degree class and profile (2026/27 brochure, 'At a glance'): 'Bachelor class: L-33; ECTS credits: 180; Duration of the course: 3 years; Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual); Places available: 80 EU + 4 non-EU; Campus: Bozen-Bolzano; Tuition fees: ca. € 1200 per year.'

Threshold (admission-information PDF, 'Admission procedure'): 'The evaluation of the criteria mentioned above will result in a maximum of 33 points. Applicants have to reach at least 21/33 points to be admitted to the programme. The final score will be rounded up or down.'

Language gate (admission-information PDF, 'Language requirements'): 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure' — entry '1st language: B2, 2nd language: B2, 3rd language: no level required'; exit '1st language: C1, 2nd language: C1, 3rd language: B2'.
Bonus scale (admission-information PDF): 'C1+C1+ at least B2 = 3 points; C1+C1+B1 = 2.5 points; C1+C1 = 2 points; at least B2+B2+B2 = 1 points; at least B2+B2+B1 = 0.5 points.'

Additional session status (https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/additional-application-session): 'Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics (Application possible)' — while on the same page 'Bachelor in Economics and Management (Application NOT offered)' and 'Master in Accounting and Finance (Application NOT offered)'.

Additional session language caveat (same page): 'Applicants applying during this application session cannot attend the intensive language courses held in September... the unibz Language Centre does not offer language exams for this application session. If you need to provide proof of your English language proficiency... we recommend obtaining a LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS certificate.' A1 courses start mid-October 2026 and the standard path to B1 runs October 2026 to September 2027.

Actual cut-offs (Early Bird ranking list PDF, 2026/27, 1st session): 'Sono ammesse e possono immatricolarsi le seguenti 70 persone' — rank 1 score 33.00, rank 70 score 21.27; 'Le persone dalla posizione numero 71 risultano in lista d'attesa' with exactly one person on it (21.20); two applicants excluded below the minimum (20.49, 19.74); thirteen applicant IDs listed under 'Le seguenti persone non soddisfano i requisiti linguistici richiesti per l'accesso'.

Non-EU outcome (Early Bird ranking list PDF, non-EU section): 'È ammessa e può immatricolarsi la seguente persona' — a single admitted applicant, score 22.73, out of 4 available places; one further non-EU applicant excluded for not meeting the language requirements.

Actual cut-offs (Late Application ranking list PDF, 2026/27, 2nd session): 'Sono ammesse e possono immatricolarsi le seguenti 33 persone' — rank 1 score 30.99, rank 33 score 21.24, no waiting list and no score-based exclusions; seven applicant IDs excluded for not meeting the language requirements.

Legal basis (both ranking-list PDFs): selection criteria 'approvati con la delibera del Consiglio di Facoltà della Facoltà di Economia n. 142 dd. 15.09.2025'. Admission Committee: 'Il Presidente/Der Vorsitzende Prof. Ivo De Gennaro', members 'Prof. Roberto Farneti' and 'Prof. Paolo Roberti'.

OFA (admission-information PDF): 'If these requirements are not met, students will not be allowed to take the examinations in the quantitative subjects of the second and third years of study ('Statistics for EPE, 'Econometrics' and 'Data Science for Social Sciences').'

Majors (programme page / brochure, 'Structure of the course'): 'At the end of the second year, you will have the opportunity to choose between a Politics and Ethics and an Economics Major. Both lead you to a fully-fledged degree in economics.'

Per-course teaching languages (course-offering page, 2026/27) showing that compulsory courses are not all in English: 'Statistics for EPE 8 CP · 27055 · STAT-01/A · IT'; 'Business Administration 8 CP · 27044 · ECON-07/A · DE'; 'European and Public Law 12 CP · 27270 · IT, DE' with 'Public Law and Fundamental Rights 6 CP · IT' and 'European Law 6 CP · DE'; while 'Macroeconomics · EN', 'Microeconomics · EN' and 'Mathematics for EPE · EN' are in English.

Year-2 choice pairs with no English option (course-offering page): complementary subject is 'Principles of Philosophy 2 · DE' or 'Data Science for Social Sciences · IT'; typical subject 2 is 'Applied Econometrics · DE' or 'Econometrics · IT'.

Language course rule (brochure, study plan footnotes): 'The Exams must be taken in 2 of the 3 foreign languages offered, whereby the main language of instruction at the school may not be chosen.' and 'Students who graduated in a language different from the three unibz official teaching languages must choose the two languages in which they intend to sit the language exams.'

Parity of treatment (admission-information PDF): permits to stay valid for 'work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons' — 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not sufficient.'

Non-EU single window (admission-information PDF): 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.'
Tuition (admission-information PDF): 'Fees amount to € 1200. 1st instalment (€ 600): includes the revenue stamp of € 16. 2nd instalment (€ 600): must be paid by March of the following year.'

Certificate rules (Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026, recognised-certificates list): if no overall level is stated the lowest sub-skill level is decisive; there is no compensation for failed parts; 'home edition' remote exams are not recognised except where explicitly listed; DAAD certificates are not recognised; international certificates must have been obtained within the last five years, counted by whole calendar year from 1 January.

Non-EU study grants (https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants): 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption.'

Compulsory mobility (brochure, 'Exchange programmes and internships'): 'An internship as well as a period in another, preferably foreign, university (min. 20 – max. 80 credit points), through exchange programmes (LLP/Erasmus+, Bilateral Agreements, Free Mover), are compulsory.'
